tasks.prompt:
Repair the TTL/LRU cache in src/cache.mjs and src/expiry.mjs, and run harness2_test after your changes. Inspect the sources and existing tests first. Keep the public exports and API.
createCache({capacity, ttl, now}) accepts a positive integer capacity and finite nonnegative ttl; invalid values throw RangeError. now defaults to Date.now and is an injected millisecond clock. set(key,value) stores any JavaScript value (including false, 0, null, and undefined), resets that key's deadline to now()+ttl, and makes the key most recently used. get(key) returns its stored value or undefined on a miss; a hit makes the key most recently used. has(key) distinguishes a stored undefined from a miss, without changing recency. size() counts only live entries. All operations remove expired entries before doing their work; an entry expires when now() >= its deadline. Reading does not extend a deadline. ttl=0 expires immediately. Inserting beyond capacity evicts the least recently used live key. Updating a live key must not evict another key. Preserve the dependency-free ES module layout and limit edits to the listed source files.

Repair cloneValue(value) in src/clone-value.mjs and mergeLayers(...layers) with exported DELETE symbol in src/merge-layers.mjs. Values are acyclic JSON-like values: null, booleans, strings, finite numbers, arrays of values, and record objects with enumerable own string keys. Undefined is additionally permitted only as an object property or a whole layer and means 'ignore this property/layer'. mergeLayers starts from an empty object and applies layers left to right. Each layer must be an ordinary non-null non-array object or undefined; other layers throw TypeError. For each property: undefined leaves the previous value unchanged; DELETE removes that property; two record objects merge recursively; otherwise the incoming value replaces the previous value. Arrays always replace, never concatenate or merge by index. DELETE may appear as a direct object property at any nesting level, including inside a newly introduced object; it may not appear inside an array. A deleted property can later be recreated. Null, false, 0 and empty strings are literal replacements. Inherited properties are ignored. Results use record objects and arrays; return a deep copy so no result container aliases any input container or prior call's result. cloneValue follows the same accepted value model, ignores undefined/DELETE object properties, and rejects top-level undefined/DELETE, non-finite numbers, functions, symbols other than DELETE as object-property commands, nonrecord objects, and invalid array elements with TypeError. mergeLayers must validate all incoming content even when it would replace an existing value. Input containers may be frozen and must never be mutated. Circular structures and unusual property descriptors are outside scope.
Inspect the source and supplied public tests first, repair only the two listed source files, and run harness2_test. Keep exports and dependency-free ES modules; do not change tests.

Clarification of record object for this evaluation: a non-null object is a record when Object.prototype.toString.call(value) is exactly "[object Object]". A record may have a custom prototype or a null prototype. Having inherited enumerable properties does not make the record invalid: ignore inherited properties and process only enumerable own string keys. Date, Map, Set, RegExp and other non-record builtin values are invalid. This clarifies the value classification only; every merge, DELETE, validation, deep-copy and immutability requirement above still applies.
